audit_findings.title: Convertible notes are treated inconsistently across numerator and denominator
audit_findings.magnitude: $172.5 million principal; 1.443 million conversion shares; $2.035 million after-tax interest for the six months ended June 30, 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: The share denominator assumes conversion, OE retains note interest, and the bridge adds the note-funded cash without deducting the note claim.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company has the right to elect to settle conversions either in cash, shares of its common stock, or in a combination of cash and shares of its common stock.
audit_findings.explanation: The inconsistency is demonstrated. Conversion shares equal about 5.8% of the 25.082 million valuation denominator, while the $172.5 million principal equals 14.7% of base equity value. Retaining interest understates value under a converted-equity convention, whereas adding the cash without recognizing the note claim overstates value under a debt convention.
audit_findings.action: Rerun under both coherent conventions: conversion shares with after-tax interest added back, and no conversion shares with the note claim deducted or otherwise matched to its associated cash.

audit_findings.title: FY2025 owner earnings may retain a nonrecurring payroll-tax credit
audit_findings.magnitude: $3.4 million net pre-tax benefit before tax effect ($4.1 million operating benefit less $0.7 million consultant fee), equal to 7.1% of the $48.0 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: An unnormalized credit raises FY2025 OE and can raise the log-trend or latest-actual anchor used throughout the forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company recorded benefits to cost of sales of $ 2.7 million, sales and marketing expenses of $ 0.8 million, general and administrative expenses of $ 0.3 million, and research and development expenses of $ 0.3 million, and interest income of $ 0.7 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The nonrecurring benefit is demonstrated, but its treatment in the OE worksheet is unresolved. Its pre-tax size is large relative to the anchor, and normalizing FY2025 could also cause the MIN(trend, latest) rule to select a lower latest-actual amount.
audit_findings.action: Trace all four operating-credit allocations and the related consultant fee through the FY2025 OE worksheet, apply the filed tax treatment, rebuild the log trend, and rerun the anchor selection.

audit_findings.title: Forecast growth may omit the acquisition investment that produced historical growth
audit_findings.mechanism: Acquisition-funded growth can enter the projected growth rate without the acquisition payments being deducted from OE as reinvestment.
audit_findings.evidence: A significant portion of our growth has been driven by acquisitions.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that acquisitions have been a significant historical growth source, but it does not quantify organic OE growth or the acquisition spending required to sustain 6%–9% growth. The issue is reasonably capable of affecting the conclusion because the supplied 0% and 6% cases differ by $225 million of equity value, or $8.96 per share.
audit_findings.action: Build organic revenue and OE growth by year, exclude acquired contributions, and rerun any growth case that cannot be supported organically with a normalized acquisition-investment charge.

audit_findings.title: Incremental working-capital requirements may be missing from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: working-capital uses of $11.3 million in 2023, $20.1 million in 2024, $1.7 million in 2025, and $12.7 million in the first half of 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: If omitted, increases in operating inventory, deferred tissue costs, receivables, and other working capital are not deducted from OE or from the reinvestment supporting forecast growth.
audit_findings.evidence: The net cash used for working capital was driven by increases in inventory and other deferred costs of $7.2 million and increases in accounts receivable of $2.9 million, offset by increases in accounts payable and other liabilities of $4.2 million, decreases in prepaid expenses and other assets of $2.4 million, and increases in accrued interest of $1.8 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed cash-flow amounts are substantial relative to the $48.0 million anchor, although annual volatility means the sustainable requirement is unresolved. An OE model that excludes normalized incremental operating working capital can materially overstate distributable cash and terminal value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile every OE year to cash-flow-statement working-capital changes, remove financing and nonoperating components such as accrued interest, estimate normalized operating working capital per unit of growth, and rerun all scenarios if it is absent.

audit_findings.title: Pending FDA reinspection could make the normalized earnings base nonrepresentative
audit_findings.mechanism: Future remediation costs, production constraints, inventory losses, or lost Artegraft sales would reduce OE and potentially sustainable growth.
audit_findings.evidence: We subsequently addressed the observations and we await reinspection for confirmation of our corrective actions.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing reports that the June 2026 reinspection produced new observations, but also states that costs have not been material to date and Artegraft sales have not been disrupted. The possible valuation effect remains forward-looking and is not presently quantified in the record.
audit_findings.action: Monitor the next FDA and company disclosures for closure of the warning letter, further observations, enforcement action, quantified remediation costs, inventory effects, or production and sales restrictions; rerun only when an operating effect is evidenced.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition-related contingent payments may be absent from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $0.989 million filed acquisition-related obligations at June 30, 2026 ($0.380 million current plus $0.609 million long-term), equal to about 0.08% of $1.172 billion base equity value and about $0.04 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Any unpaid acquisition consideration omitted from both OE and the bridge would be deducted from equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: In December 2025, we entered into an agreement with Andramed GmbH to purchase the assets of their AndraValvulotome business for $1.8 million plus additional payments of up to $0.8 million, contingent upon the passage of time and, separately, receipt of CE mark approval.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge does not expressly show these obligations, but the entire filed balance is only about 0.08% of base equity value and approximately $0.04 per diluted share, too small to change the valuation conclusion. The separately disclosed AndraValvulotome contingent maximum of $0.8 million is similarly immaterial and may already be included in the filed obligation balance.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $0.989 million filed balance to the AndraValvulotome agreement and bridge; deduct any confirmed omitted amount in the next maintenance rerun.
